metadata.name: Boris Johnson
metadata.description: UK prime minister combining Brexit sovereignty, free-trade advocacy and unionism with public-service commitments, emergency spending and a strong defence and technology agenda.
metadata.scope: Personal positions and governing conduct during 2019–2022. Coalition measures are attributed cautiously. Modern hypothetical policies are labelled inferred, not claimed as direct statements. Research cutoff 4 October 2026; later views do not overwrite a former governing period.
metadata.role: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom

axes.brief: Electoral parliamentary government remained the source of authority, despite serious conflict over scrutiny and constitutional conventions.
axes.counterEvidence: The unlawful prorogation, standards controversies and resistance to resignation weaken an unqualified democratic-accountability assessment.

answers.rationale: He sought and won a general-election mandate rather than replacing competitive elections.
Technical advisers assisted a politically accountable cabinet; they were not substitutes for the electorate.

His electoral reforms required identification but did not condition the franchise on educational attainment or intelligence. Voter-identification controversy is distinct from the educational exclusion proposed here.
His prorogation attempt weakened parliamentary scrutiny, but did not establish an unrestricted right to legislate after parliamentary rejection.
Opposition parties competed freely in 2019 despite an intensely adversarial campaign.
Accepted parliamentary opposition coexisted with conduct that obstructed scrutiny; unconditional support for its resources is less secure.
He accepted the prorogation judgment operationally while criticising judicial intervention, producing a mixed checks-and-balances record.
Trade unions had no privileged right to appoint his government instead of voters.
His confrontational rhetoric did not become a general programme to exclude lawful opposition parties from elections.
His insistence on implementing the Brexit referendum gives popular votes substantial authority, within a parliamentary legal process.
Cabinet, Parliament and party confidence remained necessary despite his personal claims to a mandate.
His eventual resignation after losing party support accepts constitutional removal, although he resisted pressure to leave.
He sought an election to resolve parliamentary deadlock rather than claiming unilateral authority to postpone voting.
Electoral accountability supports removal mechanisms, but fixed terms and parliamentary procedures qualify a universal recall right.
His leadership stretched conventions, yet electoral accountability remained a legitimate constraint he did not formally abolish.
His political programme retained civilian parliamentary government rather than military substitution.

axes.brief: Personal-liberty rhetoric coexisted with strong policing, security powers and extensive pandemic restrictions.
axes.counterEvidence: Infection-control restrictions involve harms to others; they do not alone establish unlimited paternalism over solely private health risks.

answers.rationale: His government's punitive drugs approach limits an autonomy-based presumption even for personal use.
Security and law-enforcement priorities support court-authorised surveillance of serious criminal suspects.
His public-order approach gives disruption substantial weight even when protesters preserve emergency access.
His free-expression rhetoric protects offensive criticism, although broad public-order powers complicate the practical boundary.
Pandemic restrictions demonstrate coercive health powers, but infection externalities differ from actions harming only the individual.
Expansive security powers make surveillance acceptable, while democratic oversight prevents a clear endorsement of unlimited universal tracking.
Road-safety enforcement accords with his government's preventive public-protection approach.
Court-reviewed restrictions on dangerous individuals fit his emphasis on preventive security.
His culturally permissive and free-speech positions resist prohibiting media merely because some find it immoral.
Anonymous speech protects dissent, while his online-safety approach gives weight to identification and enforcement against abuse.
His policing priorities support tightly bounded searches when credible immediate violence threatens a particular area.
His emphasis on preventing serious disruption supports proportionate advance restrictions on demonstrably dangerous gatherings.
Ordinary policing should remain legally authorised, with urgent safety exceptions rather than routine unrestricted home entry.
Journalism has an accountability role, but official secrecy and national-security interests remain substantial constraints.

The governing framework in Great Britain does not accept personal protection as a good reason for ordinary civilian firearm ownership, even after screening. The November 2022 guide confirms a longstanding policy of successive governments; narrow exceptional regimes do not establish the general permission asked here.

Strong counterterrorism powers coexist with judicial supervision of extended detention. Longer detention or exceptional security powers do not by themselves establish permission for prolonged imprisonment without independent court review.

axes.brief: Shared British civic identity and language are emphasised while multiple cultural backgrounds remain legitimate.
axes.counterEvidence: National heritage emphasis does not imply excluding all minority religious practice or forbidding ancestral identity.

answers.rationale: Shared British identity and integration have priority in his nation-building rhetoric, though not complete cultural conformity.
Accommodation is legitimate when practical, but national institutions and common expectations limit open-ended adaptation.
His integration approach expects familiarity with common language and civic customs.
British citizenship can coexist with inherited community identity in his publicly plural national account.
English proficiency is an important part of his expectations for integration.
Recognition can enrich ceremonies, but he does not generally give separate communities precedence over common national symbolism.
His defence of national heritage supports maintaining established traditions with public assistance.
His emphasis on shared national belonging resists treating separate community identity as the overriding civic priority.
A shared national calendar fits his concern with common institutions and traditions.
His public national narrative includes immigrant contributions and multiple traditions within British identity.
Integration into wider British life is central to the common identity he advocates.
Commercial freedom favours varied signage, but common-language accessibility can justify practical requirements.
Families may preserve traditions, while his integration agenda expects participation in broader national civic life.
Personal liberty weighs against banning religious dress, while general identification and security rules can justify limited exceptions.
His civic patriotism can include different cultural backgrounds without dissolving shared British institutions.
He places greater emphasis on learning common language and civic norms than on preserving separate community institutions.

axes.brief: Selective legal migration and designated humanitarian routes coexist with strict irregular-entry deterrence.
axes.counterEvidence: Hong Kong and Ukraine routes and expanded skilled pathways complicate a uniformly closed-border interpretation.

answers.rationale: His points-based system controlled eligibility but explicitly suspended the skilled-worker numerical cap. This favours selective admission rather than a strict overall annual numerical ceiling.
A wish for better living conditions alone falls short of his selective admission criteria.
His points-based system gives skills and employment a prominent role, while retaining other routes.
Family reunion remains available but is subject to financial and eligibility restrictions rather than a broad presumption.
Humanitarian schemes matter, but route restrictions and selection prevent unconditional permanent admission of all refugees.
His Rwanda policy and enforcement rhetoric strongly favour removal rather than regularisation as the default.
Domestic control and selectivity can justify restrictions despite employer demand.
Pressure on services is an accepted consideration in controlling admissions.

Family migration remained subject to eligibility rules, while the new system did not impose a single total annual cap encompassing every migrant category. Controlled admission is not evidence for the specified numerical mechanism.
Employment must satisfy salary, skill and other visa criteria; an offer alone is insufficient.

Employer and family sponsorship remained important, but humanitarian and exceptional talent routes qualify a general sponsorship requirement. Family reunion itself is not an exception here because the question already includes family sponsors.
A graduate pathway does not make completed study an unconditional entitlement to permanent residence.
Humanitarian urgency can warrant special schemes, but he favours designated controlled routes over unrestricted cap exemptions.
His selective schemes reflect particular obligations and crises, without establishing cultural resemblance as a general refugee criterion.
Restrictions on access to public funds distinguish many temporary migrants from citizens.
Cultural contribution can be welcomed, but difference itself is not the main criterion of his points-based admissions system.

axes.brief: Global military reach, NATO deterrence and increased defence capability accompany diplomatic cooperation.
axes.counterEvidence: Diplomacy and arms-control language remain part of strategy; support for military AI does not automatically mean unaccountable autonomous killing.

answers.rationale: His Global Britain posture permits force to defend wider strategic interests beyond retaliation for a direct attack.
Diplomacy remains essential, but deterrence and support for Ukraine reject indefinite accommodation merely to avoid military confrontation.
Increased defence investment and nuclear capacity prioritise credible military advantage despite fiscal pressure.
His security strategy permits preventive responses to credible imminent threats under international-law constraints.
Expeditionary capability and collective security extend beyond a strict retaliatory-only doctrine.
He relied on a professional armed force rather than universal male conscription.
Negotiation is useful, but his Ukraine position resists concessions that reward aggression merely to secure immediate peace.
Defence AI is encouraged, while the official strategy requires ethical safeguards and preserves human political control over nuclear weapons.
His international military posture explicitly requires capabilities beyond repelling attacks on British territory.
His alliance and Ukraine commitments reject avoiding war at any cost even to allied security.
Global deployments and naval reach are important parts of the defence strategy he endorsed.
Territorial disputes should usually be managed diplomatically, but his deterrence approach does not rule out force in every such conflict.
Credible military and intelligence capabilities supply bargaining power alongside diplomacy.
His response to Russian aggression gives resolve substantial weight even when confrontation increases short-term risks.
Intelligence and offensive cyber capabilities are central to his strategy despite diplomatic friction.
Arms control can improve security, but his expansion of the nuclear stockpile ceiling rejects reductions irrespective of threats.

axes.brief: Brexit sovereignty prioritises domestic control while preserving NATO, trade agreements and international cooperation.
axes.counterEvidence: Trade treaties and NATO are genuine constraints; sovereignty rhetoric does not imply total international isolation.

answers.rationale: Brexit places final domestic authority and regulatory autonomy at the centre of his programme.
He resists supranational decisions imposed despite British opposition, while accepting selected negotiated treaty obligations.
His Brexit settlement sought domestic legal autonomy from EU judicial authority.
NATO remains a valued long-term constraint accepted for collective defence.
Withdrawal from the EU exemplifies his view that international membership rests on continuing national consent.
Sovereign judicial authority and objections to external constraints limit support for binding international jurisdiction over officials.
National priorities take precedence when shared rules are judged to prevent his domestic programme.
Climate cooperation is strongly endorsed, but his preferred model retains substantial national policymaking control.
He rejects EU common foreign-policy authority while enthusiastically participating in NATO and coordinated allied action.
Rights commitments are acknowledged, but external power to require domestic legislative change conflicts with his sovereignty emphasis.
Maintaining sterling follows his resistance to political and monetary integration.
Joint projects and aid funds can be useful, but open-ended supranational budget authority conflicts with Brexit autonomy.
National border control is a central stated purpose of his post-Brexit immigration system.
He favours negotiated common trading rules, provided they preserve substantial regulatory autonomy.
His Brexit programme rejects incorporation into a larger political federation.
His free-trade agreements require compliance, while the Northern Ireland Protocol dispute shows willingness to challenge costly obligations.

axes.brief: Private enterprise remains the default, with the NHS, infrastructure and crisis interventions providing substantial public roles.
axes.counterEvidence: Furlough was income support, not state ownership. Crisis rail intervention differs from a general nationalisation programme.

answers.rationale: His programme preserves a predominantly private-enterprise economy.
Private utilities remain accepted under regulation, while public infrastructure and crisis intervention retain important roles.
Market ownership is his normal preference when service performance and public accountability are equivalent.
Industrial support does not generally imply creating state-owned firms to compete across ordinary commercial markets.
His defence of the NHS supports a substantial public-provider role rather than predominantly private health delivery.
Railway infrastructure and coordinated services warrant a significant public role, despite continued use of private contractors.
Outsourcing fits his approach when genuine cost savings preserve quality and accountability.

His government launched the taxpayer-owned UK Infrastructure Bank in June 2021 to invest alongside private finance. Its specialised infrastructure mandate supports qualified agreement without implying replacement of commercial banking.
His market orientation favours disposing of ordinary commercial holdings when no strategic public rationale remains.
Public and social housing can help supply, but private construction and ownership remain major instruments.
Private strategic firms remain acceptable when regulation and security conditions adequately protect public interests.
His economic framework generally leaves extraction to regulated private companies rather than universal public ownership.
Local contracting is compatible with his preference for competition and practical service efficiency.
Strategic control can justify retention, though neither cash receipts nor state ownership always takes precedence.
Persistent commercial losses strengthen the case for sale unless a demonstrable essential public function requires support.
Public-service media has value, but his government's Channel 4 privatisation plans weaken a presumption of permanent national ownership.

axes.brief: Explicit free-trade advocacy coexists with post-Brexit barriers and strategic security exceptions.
axes.counterEvidence: Leaving the single market increased barriers despite liberalising rhetoric; answer values distinguish stated trade preferences from sovereignty tradeoffs.

answers.rationale: His Greenwich speech explicitly attacks tariff protection and celebrates international exchange.
His free-trade programme accepts competitive pressure on domestic firms to expand wider prosperity.
National procurement priorities coexist with a stated preference for open competition and access to imports.
Access to competitively priced foreign inputs follows his argument for comparative advantage.
Strategic resilience can justify exceptions, but his trade argument resists routine restriction of cheaper essential imports.
Independent tariff policy can reduce barriers, although negotiated reciprocal agreements were his principal practical method.
Support for strategic emerging sectors is possible, but broad protection of infant firms conflicts with his competition rhetoric.
Inward investment is encouraged subject to strategic security screening.
Agricultural producers receive support, but his trade-deal agenda accepts greater import competition.
Adjustment and investment fit his pro-trade strategy more closely than permanent protection for every displaced producer.
He condemns tariff escalation while accepting lawful trade remedies; retaliation depends on proportionality and strategic context.
Nondiscriminatory market access follows his argument against using domestic regulation as disguised trade exclusion.
His support for fair trading conditions permits targeted remedies against demonstrable subsidy distortions.
His pursuit of post-Brexit agreements favours tariff removal despite greater trading interdependence.
Strategic investment screening can prevent foreign control where national security is credibly threatened.
His digital-hub ambitions favour cross-border digital commerce within security and consumer-protection rules.

axes.brief: Markets allocate most production, supplemented by wage floors, infrastructure, industrial subsidies and emergency support.
axes.counterEvidence: Exceptional pandemic direction should not be treated as the normal preferred economic system.

answers.rationale: Private enterprise ordinarily determines production in his market-based programme.
Emergency pandemic coordination does not establish compulsory output targets as normal economic practice.
Competitive prices are generally preferred, with exceptional essential-service safeguards.
Infrastructure and green-industry programmes direct investment toward selected sectors.
Consumer demand and commercial opportunity normally determine business expansion and exit.
Temporary essential-price intervention can be justified, but general price administration conflicts with his market programme.
New firms ordinarily need to meet lawful standards rather than prove a government-defined production need.
Public development finance can target priorities, while ordinary bank lending remains commercially determined.
Open capital flows support his global financial-centre strategy, subject to sanctions and security restrictions.
Levelling-up and green investment accept selective subsidies for strategic objectives.
Financial innovation is encouraged, but official monetary stability and regulatory oversight constrain unrestricted private money.
His defence of Britain's statutory wage floor supports continued national minimum-wage regulation.
Wage floors coexist with employer and worker negotiation rather than comprehensive official wage schedules.
Independent monetary policy is compatible with his programme; a binding production plan directing the central bank is not.
Private rental pricing remains broadly market-based, supplemented by housing support and tenant protections.
Crisis support and infrastructure spending do not imply routine national direction of ordinary production and distribution.

axes.brief: Levelling-up and expanded services coexist with work incentives, property rights and restrained permanent redistribution.
axes.counterEvidence: National Insurance and corporation-tax increases complicate a simple small-state interpretation; the Universal Credit uplift was temporary.

answers.rationale: Levelling-up supports reducing disadvantage, while his market orientation and work incentives qualify large permanent equalisation.
Differences in income are not alone sufficient to justify every additional tax under his enterprise-based approach.
NHS and social-care funding demonstrate willingness to raise contributions for essential protection.
His emphasis is on opportunity and services more than systematically narrowing every income gap.
Progressive taxation remains accepted, despite rhetorical commitments to lower burdens.
Rewards for enterprise and work retain weight even when incomes remain unequal.
Inherited opportunity matters, but his governing programme did not make major estate redistribution a central instrument.

Universal Credit retained ongoing means-tested eligibility and work-related conditions rather than an automatic lifetime expiry merely because unemployment had lasted too long. Sanctions for noncompliance are distinct from the fixed time cutoff in this statement.
Broad annual wealth taxation is inconsistent with his main fiscal instruments and investment incentives.
Fiscal restraint competes with expanded health, infrastructure and temporary crisis support.
Public health care and support for participation imply more than subsistence-only protection.
Tax-cut ambitions coexist with tax increases for public services, preventing an unconditional tax-first ordering.
In-work support and changes to Universal Credit incentives fit a work-focused social minimum.
Retaining progressive bands conflicts with an equal marginal tax rate for everyone.
Property-rights and homeownership priorities weigh against broad compulsory land redistribution even with compensation.
Work incentives constrain benefits, but health and disability support extend beyond emergency basic survival.

axes.brief: Secular civil authority coexists with an established church and customary religious ceremony.
axes.counterEvidence: Personal religious history is not the basis of the score; established institutions and civil-law practice are.

answers.rationale: Secular public reasons matter, while established Christian institutions retain constitutional and ceremonial standing.
His laws are not generally derived from religious doctrine despite Christian cultural references.
Civil parliamentary authority does not depend on clerical approval.
He accepted the established Church rather than advocating a constitution without official religious status.
Teaching knowledge about religions is consistent with public education and plural citizenship.
Faith schools and collective worship coexist with exemptions and plural provision, rather than one mandatory national faith curriculum.
Civil law takes precedence even while religious institutions retain protected autonomy.

The retained Lords Spiritual have an official role scrutinising and voting on legislation. They need not possess a religious veto for this to constitute the review role asked about; civil institutions still make the final law.
Official worship and religious ceremonies remained accepted parts of national public life.
Faith-based social provision merits support, but funding persuasion into belief has a weaker public justification.
Established symbols are accepted, while exclusive religious citizenship would conflict with his plural national account.
Christian public holidays fit his preservation of national traditions without requiring personal observance.
Continued episcopal seats in the Lords conflict with excluding all clerical representation.
Charitable tax treatment can include religious bodies without establishing unrestricted privileges solely for belief.
Civil marriage remains accessible independently of religious approval.
Religious practice does not supersede civil family-law rights or ordinary courts.

axes.brief: Socially permissive positions coexist with heritage, gradualism and caution on contested identity policy.
axes.counterEvidence: Transgender policy became more restrictive than earlier equality rhetoric; general social permissiveness is therefore qualified.

answers.rationale: His socially liberal record allows customs to change rather than treating inherited arrangements as immutable.
National tradition has value, but he also accepts substantial changes to family and social life.
Recognition of diverse families fits his support for existing equality protections.

His support for women in employment and public leadership weighs against government encouragement of a universal male-provider and female-carer norm. Voluntary traditional households remain compatible with this qualified disagreement.
He supported legal same-sex marriage and retained that position in office.
Stable family life is valued, but formal preference cannot readily exclude other legally recognised families.
His government maintained legal abortion access, though regulatory safeguards and devolved differences complicate an unlimited reading.
Parental involvement deserves weight while schools retain duties to teach basic relationships and equality.
Same-sex parental eligibility follows his support for legal family equality, subject to child-welfare standards.

His socially permissive conduct and acceptance of personal dress choices coexist with conventional expectations of context-appropriate public behaviour. Neither a general state-backed modesty standard nor complete rejection of social convention follows from that mixture.
Courtesy and inclusion matter, while his free-speech posture resists treating every contested language preference as compulsory.
Inherited standards can inform judgment, but he does not consistently require them to prevail over contemporary equality claims.
Equal occupational opportunity is compatible with his programme and does not depend on conforming to traditional gender roles.
Institutional caution and consensus can favour gradual change even when reform has substantial support.
Inclusive teaching is legitimate, while age appropriateness and parental concerns remain relevant.
Heritage has value partly through continuity, even where every custom lacks an immediate practical purpose.

axes.brief: A science-superpower agenda favours innovation, coupled with regulatory and environmental safeguards.
axes.counterEvidence: Specific brain-implant and embryo-enhancement answers are explicit extrapolations, not claims of documented personal positions.

answers.rationale: His science-superpower agenda favours early adoption and substantial investment despite unresolved long-term uncertainties.

His innovation agenda favoured accelerated development and proportionate risk-based approval rather than generally awaiting substantial long-term risk evidence. This is qualified disagreement with that timing threshold, not rejection of trials or a claim that the question demands certainty.
Infrastructure and growth priorities can justify limited habitat losses after assessment and mitigation.
Vaccine acceleration demonstrates willingness to shorten timelines when benefits are urgent, without abandoning safety evidence.
AI investment and skills policy favour adoption coupled with workforce adaptation.
Biodiversity commitments constrain development, but do not automatically defeat projects with substantial public benefit.
His science-based food and biotechnology position plausibly favours regulated innovation over a general long-term precautionary ban.
Biomedical ambition supports trials, while invasive enhancement risks justify a higher threshold than ordinary consumer technology.
His green industrial strategy strongly favours technological decarbonisation rather than relying primarily on reduced consumption.
Environmental review matters, but development priorities resist open-ended delay for every uncertain effect.
Voluntary choice matters, yet invasive implants require robust regulation beyond an assumption that basic safety resolves long-term risk.
Responsible AI commitments imply clinical validation and safeguards against errors before routine medical deployment.
Scientific opportunity warrants research, while irreversible heritable effects justify strict consent and safety constraints.

His science and development agenda favoured managed deployment with targeted environmental safeguards rather than a general prerequisite of extensive long-term ecosystem studies. The issue is the evidence threshold and timing, not whether all ecosystem risk can be eliminated.
Housing and transport provision receive substantial priority when environmental harms can be mitigated.

Innovation and military-technology policy accepted managed risks for substantial benefits while recognising accountability and serious-harm safeguards. These considerations support a conditional balance on requiring strong evidence against irreversible harm; the statement asks for low risk, not zero risk.

axes.brief: Strong UK central authority and unionism constrain the autonomy of devolved governments.
axes.counterEvidence: Pandemic policy remained devolved and mayors retained powers; centralism was substantial but not complete abolition of local government.

answers.rationale: His muscular unionism gives devolved disagreement less protection when it frustrates UK-wide objectives.
Parliamentary sovereignty and the Internal Market Act give national institutions broad final authority.
His opposition to a further Scottish independence referendum rejects an automatic unilateral regional secession right.
UK-wide market and spending measures show willingness to override devolved objections.
Devolved institutions are accepted, but their constitutional protection is weaker than autonomous regional constitutions beyond Westminster control.
Police powers remain substantially devolved, though national security and common enforcement priorities justify coordination.
National redistribution and direct UK spending contradict a presumption that each region retains most locally collected revenue.
England-wide standards are supported, but education remained devolved in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
Local fiscal choice exists within strong national limits rather than broad independent taxing power.
National wage floors and employment law establish common rules across much of the union.
Local arrangements deserve flexibility, but central statutes define and constrain council powers.

England-wide NHS guarantees coexisted with devolved health policy and differing coverage decisions elsewhere in the UK. Common national commitments therefore do not establish uniform central control over every region.
Recognition of distinct communities does not clearly imply constitutionally autonomous Indigenous political institutions in his unitary framework.
National fiscal coherence and funding equalisation justify limits on destabilising regional tax competition.
Local impact supports local voice, but his planning agenda accepts central intervention for wider development objectives.

His union-wide coordination agenda favours a central emergency role, but the pandemic retained distinct devolved powers and policies. That governing compromise supports qualified rather than absolute central control.

axes.brief: Educational and institutional explanations receive weight, with mixed causal judgments where neither nature nor nurture predominates clearly.
axes.counterEvidence: Equality commitments cannot establish scientific heritability. Mixed answers avoid asserting either universal environmental causation or racial biological hierarchy.

answers.rationale: His emphasis on education and opportunity coexists with acceptance of differing aptitudes; neither establishes one universal causal predominance.
His government frames national prosperity through institutions and skills rather than inherited national intelligence hierarchies.
Equal opportunity is compatible with both social and biological influences on average behaviour; policy alone cannot establish their relative magnitude.
Individual stress responses plausibly reflect physiology and circumstances; his health approach supplies reasons to consider both.
Skills and educational investment assume experience can substantially redirect interests and achievement.
Enterprise rhetoric recognises individual dispositions, while opportunity and incentives also alter risk-taking.
Civic institutions and shared expectations can cultivate cooperation within his integration-based national account.
Empathy plausibly reflects disposition and socialisation; no causal dominance follows from his national-community rhetoric.
Education and skills policy treats learning environments as consequential for attention and performance.
Traditional moral attachment and adaptation to social change supply competing reasons, not proof of predominantly biological moral reactions.
Security responses recognise objective threats, while integration and civic contact can alter learned perceptions; both channels matter.
Individual differences may have biological components, while educational development prevents treating temperament as fixed biological destiny.

His combination of individual dispositions and education-based opportunity supports a mixed analogy for aesthetic preferences: bodily attraction and learned social tastes can both matter. Opposition to conversion therapy concerns sexual orientation and cannot establish this different causal claim.

Integration, education and policing policy give social conditions a substantial role in explaining racial crime disparities. This warrants a modest inference against biological predominance; citizenship equality alone cannot establish the complete causal account.
Investment in schooling and opportunity makes learned self-regulation more plausible than racial determinism.
Preferences can affect careers, but equality protections acknowledge discrimination and social expectations; neither is dismissed as irrelevant.

review.notes: Independent review of all 240 exact questions for the 2019–2022 premiership. Corrected the personal-defence firearm answer from strong permission to strong disagreement using the longstanding GB rule; screening is not sufficient. Corrected annual immigration cap mechanisms using the removal of the skilled-worker cap, and distinguished family sponsorship from an unsponsored route. Added the actual 2021 public Infrastructure Bank; corrected church legislative review versus veto and welfare conditionality versus automatic time expiry. Distinguished court review from detention length, education tests from voter identification, devolved health powers from English standards, and physical attractiveness from sexual orientation. Repaired innovation risk-evidence rhetoric and moderated causal and central-emergency certainty. November 2022 firearms guidance is used retrospectively only for its expressly longstanding rule, not as a new Johnson act. Modern hypotheticals and causal anthropology remain qualified inferences. No target distribution or similarity score was used; batch similarity remains separate. Integration review by OpenAI Codex /root on 2026-10-04: portrait identity, local rendering, size and Commons attribution checked; the shared Image credits list includes this source. All 35 requested profiles were compared using calculated scores, with any resemblance at or above 95% explicitly reviewed against the named revision. Neutral-count warnings were retained only after the evidence review; they are not missing answers. Portrait integration review by OpenAI Codex on 2026-10-04: verified the Wikipedia infobox file, Commons creator and reuse status, and image size. The independent political evidence audit is retained; no political assessment changed.
